clue.text: Chilling result sees United going back down

indicators.note: going back tells us the word for united is read from right to left

parts.note: united in marriage means wed
to drop is to go down

explanation.surface: A news report notes the football team, Manchester United, has slipped down the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns WED (united) into DEW. 'United' looks like a football club, but here it means joined in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew forms when air cools overnight, so a single bead of it is the result of a chill.

clue.text: Fool's exercise?

definitions.meaning: a fool is a dimwit or idiot
the question mark flags this split reading

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'. The second definition splits the answer into DO + PE, 'do PE' being the same as 'exercise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal for a stupid person, and split in two it reads as an instruction to do gym class.

clue.text: Took gross delight in being amazed about everything

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, surrounding it

parts.note: to be wowed is to be amazed
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone revelled crudely while being astonished by it all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as revelling in astonishment; 'about' is the container signal, and 'being' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallow is to indulge yourself in something without restraint, taking coarse pleasure in it.

clue.text: Ringing provides motive with a flying insect

indicators.note: flying here means flying off, so the letter is taken away from the word for motive

parts.note: a motive is a reason for doing something
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Something resonant gives a reason, along with a buzzing bug flying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' makes it look like the insect is the flying one; in fact it is 'a' that flies away from REASON, leaving RESON. 'provides' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is deep and echoing, the kind that keeps ringing on.

clue.text: Polecat's old and cold away from fold

indicators.note: away from tells us the letters for old and cold are removed from the animal's name

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A polecat, aged and chilly, wanders away from its pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like an animal pen, matching the polecat, but it is the definition: a fold in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed or sewn into cloth.

clue.text: French group to mediate in noisy quarrel

parts.note: ACAS, the Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, is the British body that mediates in industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A team of French go-betweens steps in to settle a loud argument.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British public body that mediates between employers and unions. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl.

clue.text: Assistance in rising above the general level

definitions.meaning: aid or help given in need
standing out from a flat surface, as carving does

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. The second sense is the relief of sculpture or maps, where shapes stand up from the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief means both help for the needy and the raised projection of a design from its surface.

clue.text: What one should do to names making profit

definitions.text: What one should do to names
definitions.meaning: proper names are written with an initial capital letter
to take advantage of something and gain from it

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a spelling rule; the second is the business sense, as in 'capitalise on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitalise is both to give a word its upper-case first letter and to turn something to financial advantage.

clue.text: Flexible workers start to teach addition

parts.note: supple means flexible, bending easily
men is a common crossword word for workers

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Agile staff begin teaching an extra course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes T, the first letter of 'teach'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement is something added to complete or enhance a whole, an extra part.

clue.text: Jetty with only one remaining central column

indicators.note: central says one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
the last is the only one remaining when all others have gone

explanation.surface: A jetty is left with just one central supporting post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' is the container signal, putting the run for the last survivor into the middle of the jetty word, just after its first two letters. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall, a kind of column in architecture.

clue.text: Opposite of beginner's error

indicators.note: opposite of tells us to read the word for beginners the other way round

parts.note: pupils are learners or beginners; the 's is read as a plural S

explanation.surface: The reverse of a novice's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite of' turns PUPILS backwards into SLIPUP. 'beginner's' looks possessive, but the 's supplies the plural letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a minor mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Gathered on line as shellfish might

indicators.note: gathered means understood or heard, and on line means over the telephone, so the next word is taken as heard spoken

parts.note: a mussel is a shellfish

explanation.surface: Shellfish could be gathered on a rope line, as mussels are farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mussels being harvested from ropes; read instead 'gathered' as heard and 'on line' as over the phone, so the shellfish's name is heard as a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical strength or power, just as might does.

clue.text: Helpful piece that needs no words

definitions.meaning: playing a useful part in bringing something about
a piece of music without vocals or lyrics

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is as in 'instrumental in the deal'; the second is music played without singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Instrumental means both serving as a means to an end and describing music performed without voices.

clue.text: Beware bird flying between poles in the countryside

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are scattered through the air and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a bird darting between rural telegraph poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' fits the bird in the surface but signals the anagram. The definition describes what is strung between fence posts on farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbed wire is the spiked fencing wire stretched between posts around fields.

clue.text: Tedious formality as revolutionary spots soldier's head

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for spots is read backwards

parts.note: dots are spots
GI is an American soldier; the 's is a link
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A rebel picks out the stiff, dull ceremony of an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel, but it reverses DOTS into STOD. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodginess is dull heaviness and stuffiness, the quality of tedious formality.

clue.text: Showing up with a surprisingly decent tan

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone appears with an unexpectedly respectable suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges A DECENT TAN. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the act of being present, of turning up somewhere.

clue.text: The unevasive retreat restricts line of approach

indicators.note: retreat means the letters go backwards
restricts means the answer is held within the words, confined by them

explanation.surface: A candid person backs off, imposing limits on the approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricts' points to the letters EUNEVA inside 'The unevasive', and 'retreat' turns them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road, and figuratively a way of approaching a problem.

clue.text: Introduced to the fold with uproar in 1917

indicators.note: in 1917 tells us the word for uproar is written into entry 19 then 17, so read in the grid order 17, 19 its halves swap

parts.note: bedlam means uproar or chaos

explanation.surface: Sheep were brought into the pen amid the turmoil of the Russian Revolution year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1917 looks like a date but is the entry numbers 19 and 17: BED goes in 19 and LAM in 17, so the answer reads LAMBED. The fold is a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: When a ewe has lambed, newborn lambs have been brought into the flock.

clue.text: Issue preserved by cold bird in statement

indicators.note: in statement means the words are spoken aloud, as in a statement

parts.note: chilled food is kept fresh by cold; a wren is a small bird

explanation.surface: An announcement concerns a refrigerated songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in statement' says CHILLED WREN is spoken, giving a sound-alike. 'Issue' is offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for offspring, a person's descendants.

clue.text: See 17
Hide shorts in Bierkellar?

parts.note: German beer cellar setting: the German words for leather and trousers combine, so the hide is leather, not concealment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' seems a verb about concealing shorts; it is leather. In German Leder is leather and Hosen trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are traditional leather shorts worn in Bavaria, where beer cellars are found.

clue.text: When he leaves, they talk long and loud?

definitions.text: When he leaves, they talk long and loud?

indicators.note: leaves means the letters of the pronoun depart from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
to rant is to talk long and loud

explanation.surface: Once the oppressor has gone, the people speak out freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' signals the deletion of the pronoun. Read whole, the clue says that after the despot departs the people at last speak out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel ruler whose departure would let the oppressed sound off.

clue.text: Assembled tediously for amateurish work

indicators.note: assembled suggests the letters are put together into something new

explanation.surface: Flat-pack furniture put together slowly makes for home-made handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembled' rearranges TEDIOUSLY and FOR, apt given flat-pack furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-it-yourself is home improvement done by non-professionals.

clue.text: Visionary holds against being cut off

indicators.note: holds means one word contains the other

parts.note: a seer is a visionary, a prophet
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A prophet resists being isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts V inside SEER. 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut something off or apart.

clue.text: Old country of Asia Minor

indicators.note: of says the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: An ancient land in Anatolia.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'Asia Minor'. Siam is the former name of Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was the name of Thailand until 1939, so it is a former country name.

clue.text: See 2
Chat about following that is cold-hearted means to suppress rising

indicators.note: following means the turned word comes after the other piece
hearted means the letter for cold goes into the heart of the abbreviation

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: about means the word for chat is turned round

parts.note: to gab is to chat

explanation.surface: Chatting about callous behaviour as a way to keep feelings down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold-hearted' puts C into the middle of IE, giving ICE; 'about' turns the chat word round, and 'following' places it after. 'rising' is a swelling, not getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bag is held against a bump to reduce swelling.

clue.text: Done to contend with big picture

parts.note: over means done or finished
to vie is to contend

explanation.surface: Finished competing with a huge painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a broad general survey, the big picture.

clue.text: Artificial product of numbers at zero

indicators.note: product of means the letters come out of the following words

explanation.surface: Something fake is the result of figures at nought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' suggests multiplying numbers by zero; it means the letters are drawn from 'numbers at zero'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute, an artificial imitation.

clue.text: Men dare to change what Windscale was

indicators.note: to change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are bold enough to rebrand the nuclear site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges MEN DARE. Windscale, the British nuclear plant in Cumbria, was renamed Sellafield in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscale was given a new name, Sellafield, after a notorious fire.
